whatItDoes: Bump a repo's dependencies on a schedule without a human driving each one. A coding agent clones the repo into a sandbox, upgrades, and runs your real test suite; it pushes only when the build is green and holds majors for review.
longDescription:
You give it a repo and a schedule. On each tick a coding agent clones the repo into a fresh sandbox and bumps its dependencies, then the agent run re-attaches that same sandbox and runs your real test suite in it. What happens next depends entirely on the result: a red build is archived and dropped, a green build gets a model risk assessment of the changed dependencies, and only a green build within your risk bar gets pushed.

The graph is `plan → bump → verify → assess → publish | held | rejected`. `bump` (`models.coding`) is a long-running coding agent, so the agent run suspends at $0 while it works and resumes only when it finishes. `verify` (`sandboxes.exec`) installs and tests in the sandbox — a non-zero exit routes straight to `rejected`. `assess` (`models.run`) rates the upgrade low/medium/high; anything above `maxAutoRisk` is `held` for a human instead of pushed. Every outcome — published, held, or rejected — writes a triage report to file storage (`fileStorage.upload`), so you keep a durable record of what changed and why it did or didn't ship.

The push is the only irreversible step, so it sits behind a `dryRun` guard: with `dryRun: true` every step runs but the push and the report upload are skipped, so you can inspect the routing without changing the repo or storing a report.

You pay for the coding agent's run, the sandbox time your tests take, and the one risk-assessment model call — a dry run costs nothing beyond the coding run it still performs.
notes:
Click **Use this template** — Sapiom builds and deploys it for you; open it on the **Agents** page and run it. Your $5 signup credit covers first runs.

Give it a `repoSlug` — an in-network repo the coding agent clones and upgrades. There is deliberately no default: a repository has to exist, and a run without one stops immediately and says so rather than failing partway through. Set `testCommand` (default `npm test`) and `installCommand` (default `npm install`) to match the project, and `maxAutoRisk` (default `medium`) to control what pushes on its own versus what waits for you. To run it on a cadence, attach the `schedule` as a cron trigger on the deployed agent. Pass `dryRun: true` to trace the whole graph without pushing or uploading anything.

Prefer to work from the code? Run it locally with `run_local` (pass your own repo slug plus `"dryRun": true`) to trace plan → bump → verify → assess → publish with no Sapiom capability spend — capabilities are stubbed and the push is skipped — or edit and deploy it with the Sapiom MCP.

settings.label: Repository to upgrade
settings.description: An in-network repo the coding agent clones and upgrades. Without one the run stops immediately and says nothing was cloned.

output.detail: No `repoSlug` was given, so there was no repository to upgrade and nothing was cloned, tested, or pushed. Create an in-network repo (`git_create_repo`) or point `repoSlug` at one you already have, then re-run.

examples.title: A dry-run triage of your repo's upgrade

output.summary: Patch and minor bumps across dev dependencies; no major versions, narrow blast radius.

zeroSetup.narrative: Runs a coding agent to triage upgrades and writes a report; pushes nothing (no repo).
